questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Metagenesis is seen in
questions.solution: Cnidarians exhibit two basic body forms called polyp and medusa. The former is a sessile and cylindrical form like Hydra, Adamsia, etc. whereas, the latter is umbrella-shaped and free-swimming like Aurelia or jellyfish. Those cnidarians which exist in both forms exhibit alternation of generation (Metagenesis), i.e., polyps produce medusae asexually and medusae form the polyps sexually (e.g.& Obelia).

In phylum Aschelminthes (Nemathelminthes) the circulatory system and respiratory system are absent.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In contrast to annelids, the Platyhelminthes show

Unlike other bilaterians, they are& acoelomates& (having no& body cavity), and have no specialized& circulatory& and respiratory& organs, which restricts them to having flattened shapes that allow& oxygen& and nutrients to pass through their bodies by& diffusion. questions.subject: Botany

questions.solution: Bones of class aves are pneumatic. These bones contain air cavities to reduce body weight, thus they aid in flight.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Adult annelids have symmetry similar to that of
questions.solution: Animals like annelids, arthropods, chordates, larvae of echinoderms, etc., where the body can be divided into identical left and right halves in only one plane, exhibit bilateral symmetry. When any plane passing through the central axis of the body divides the organism into two identical halves, it is called radial symmetry. Coelenterates, ctenophores, and echinoderms have this kind of body plan. Sponges are mostly asymmetrical, i.e., any plane that passes through the center does not divide them into equal halves.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Cold-blooded animals fall under the category of
questions.solution: Ectotherms (poikilotherms) are the organisms that maintain body temperature by absorbing heat from the surrounding environment. All animals except mammals and birds are ectotherms. They are often described as being cold-blooded and are unable to regulate their body temperature metabolically.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In vertebrates, the notochord is modified into
questions.solution: The members of subphylum vertebrata possess notochord during the embryonic period. The notochord is replaced by a cartilaginous or bony vertebral column in the adult. questions.solution: In viviparous animals, females give birth to young ones. The development of zygote takes place inside the female's body. Females deliver young ones and the chances of survival of offsprings are more.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is considered a living fossil?
questions.solution: A living fossil is an organism (such as a horseshoe crab, king crab, Tuatara, Coelcanth or a ginkgo tree) that has remained essentially unchanged from earlier geologic times and whose close relatives are usually extinct. Limulus is commonly called king crab.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: An undifferentiated layer, mesoglea, is present in
questions.solution: Animals in which the cells are arranged in two embryonic layers, external ectoderm, and internal endoderm, are called diploblastic& animals, e.g., coelenterates. An undifferentiated& layer, mesoglea, is present in between the& ectoderm and the endoderm.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which is the common character between all the mammals?
questions.solution: The most unique mammalian characteristic is the presence of milk-producing glands (mammary glands) by which the young ones are nourished. They have two pairs of limbs, adapted for walking, running, climbing, burrowing, swimming, or flying. The skin of mammals& is unique in possessing hair. External ears or pinnae are present. Different types of teeth are present in the jaw. The heart is four-chambered. The presence of seven cervical vertebrae.& They are homoiothermic. Respiration is by lungs. Reptiles are classified under division Gnathostomata and superclass Tetrapoda. The class name Reptilia refers to their creeping or crawling mode of locomotion (Latin, repere or reptum, to creep or crawl). They are mostly terrestrial animals and their body is covered by dry and cornified skin, epidermal scales, or scutes. They do not have external ear openings. Tympanum represents ear. Limbs, when present, are two pairs. The heart is usually three-chambered, but four-chambered in crocodiles. Reptiles are poikilotherms. Snakes and lizards shed their scales as skin cast. Sexes are separate. Fertilization is internal. They are oviparous and development is direct.

Examples: Chelone (Turtle), Testudo (Tortoise), Chameleon (Tree lizard),& Calotes (Garden lizard), Crocodilus (Crocodile), Alligator (Alligator). Hemidactylus (Wall lizard), Poisonous snakes – Naja (Cobra), Bangarus (Krait), Vipera (Viper).

questions.solution:
Annelida exhibit an organ-system level of body organization and bilateral symmetry. They are triploblastic, metamerically segmented, and coelomate animals. Their body surface is distinctly marked out into segments or metameres and, hence, the phylum name Annelida (Latin, annulus : little ring). They possess longitudinal and circular muscles that help in locomotion. Aquatic annelids like Nereis possess lateral appendages, parapodia, which help in swimming. A closed circulatory system is present. Nephridia (sing. nephridium) helps in osmoregulation and excretion. The neural system consists of paired ganglia (sing. ganglion) connected by lateral nerves to a double ventral nerve cord. Nereis, an aquatic form, is dioecious, but earthworms and leeches are monoecious. Reproduction is sexual.

Examples: Nereis, Pheretima (Earthworm), and Hirudinaria (Bloodsucking leech).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Phylum Level of organization Digestive system Respiratory system
Aschelminthes A Complete Absent
Echinodermata Organ system B Present
Platyhelminthes Organ Incomplete C
Annelida Organ system Incomplete D


Select the option with correct identification of A, B, C, and D.
options: A - organ, B - Complete, C-Present, D - Absent
A - organ system, B - Complete , C - Absent , D - Absent
A - organ system, B - Incomplete , C - Absent , D - Present
A - organ system, B - Incomplete , C - Present , D - Absent
questions.solution:
I. Levels of the organization - It is of various types

A. Cellular level - Division of labour is there between the cells but are not tissues. These are in the form of loose cell aggregates. Example: Sponges (Porifers)

B. Tissue level - Cells that are organized to perform the same function act as tissues. Examples: Coelenterates.

C. Organ level - Tissues grouped together to form organs. Examples: Platyhelminthes.

D. Organ system level - Organs associated to form functional systems. Examples: Annelids, arthropods, molluscs, echinoderms, and chordates.

II. Digestive system is

A. Incomplete with a single opening (blind sac body plan) that acts as anus and mouth both. e.g. Coelenterates and Platyhelminthes.

B. Complete with two openings (tube within tube plan) which behave as anus and mouth separately. e.g. from Aschelminthes up to Chordates.

III. Specific respiratory structures and respiratory system is well developed from phylum Arthropoda.

questions.solution: Though all members of Animalia are multicellular, all of them do not exhibit the same pattern of organisation of cells. For example, in sponges, the cells are arranged as loose cell aggregates, i.e., they exhibit cellular level of organisation. In coelenterates, the arrangement of cells is more complex. Here the cells performing the same function are arranged into tissues, hence is called tissue level of organisation. Organ level is exhibited by members of Platyhelminthes and other higher phyla where tissues are grouped together to form organs, each specialised for a particular function.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Identify true statements:

(A) Cnidarians have blind-sac body plan.
(B) Digestion in Ctenophora is both intra as well as extracellular
(C) Agnathans are endoparasites on fishes.
(D) Ichthyophis belongs to Tetrapoda group
questions.solution:
Cnidarians have blind-sac body plan (in this plan, the body is sac-like with a digestive cavity which opens to outside by only one aperture, which functions as mouth and anus).

In Ctenophora, digestion is both extracellular and intracellular and wastes are voided (removed) via both the mouth and the anus.

Ichthyophis is a genus of caecilians, belongs to Tetrapoda group (limbless amphibians, sometimes called the Asian caecilians) found in Southeast Asia, the southern Philippines, and the western Indo-Australian Archipelago.

Agnathans have only one living class identified called& Cyclostomata. All living members of the class Cyclostomata are ectoparasites on some fishes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following animals have different symmetry in comparison to the other three?
questions.solution:
Types of animals on the basis of symmetry -

A. Asymmetrical - No particular symmetry. Examples - Most of the sponges

B. Radially symmetrical - When any plane passing through the central axis of the body divides the organism into 2 equal halves. Examples - Few sponges, coelenterates, ctenophores and adult echinoderms.

C. Bilaterally symmetrical - If the body of an organism is divisible into 2 equal halves only in one plane. Examples - Platyhelminthes, aschelminthes, annelids, arthropods, molluscs, the larva of echinoderms and chordates.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is not applicable for members of the phylum Echinodermata?
options: Body system - Presence of canal system due to the folding of the body wall
questions.solution: Canal system due to foldings of body wall is the feature of sponges (members of Phylum Porifera). The most important feature of echinoderms is presence of water vascular system. It performs the function of locomotion, capture and transport of food.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following statements is incorrect about phylum Hemichordata?
options: Have a rudimentary structure in the collar region called stomochord.
questions.solution:
Phylum Hemichordata has been recently given the status of separate phylum because it lacks a true notochord. It was previously considered as subphylum under the Phylum Chordata.& All are marine with bilaterally symmetrical, organ system level of organization, triploblastic, and eucoelomate. The body is made up of anterior proboscis, collar, and a long trunk. Respiration by gills, the circulatory system is of open type. Excretion is by proboscis glands, dioecious and fertilization is external, development is indirect.

Examples : Balanoglossus (Tongueworm), Saccoglosssus.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Select the correct statement.
options: Arthropoda is the largest class of kingdom Animalia.
Closed type of circulatory system is found in annelids.
Psittacula is the National bird of India.
questions.solution:
Circulatory system may be of:
I. Open type: Cell and tissues directly bath into the blood, e.g., Arthropods.
II. Closed type: Blood always remain in capillaries or other blood vessels but never come in direct contact of blood., e.g., Annelids and Chordates.

questions.subject: Botany

questions.solution: Presence of mammary gland is a characteristic feature of the members of Class Mammalia. Pteropus, also known as a flying fox, is a mammal.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Metagenesis or alteration of generation can be observed in members of phylum
questions.solution:
Metagenesis (or alternation of generation) Coelenterates exhibit two body forms: polyp and medusa.

A. Polyp = Sessile and cylindrical like Hydra, Adamsia.

B. Medusa = Free swimming, umbrella shaped like Aurelia (jelly fish). Those cnidarians in which both polyp and medusa alternates with each other, are said to exhibit metagenesis. During metagenesis, polyp (asexual stage) reproduce asexually to form medusa, whereas the medusa (sexual stage) sexually reproduce to form polyp, e.g., Obelia.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Phylum Mollusca is characterized by
questions.solution: Molluscs are triploblastic, bilaterally symmetrical coelomates. In some Molluscs like Pila, due to torsion during growth, the adults become asymmetrical. The coelom& is greatly reduced. It is restricted to the pericardial cavity (space around the heart), and to small spaces within kidneys and gonads (testes and ovaries). Spaces amongst the viscera (soft organs) contain blood and form hemocoel. They have triploblastic body wall with outer ectoderm middle mesoderm and inner endoderm.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Respiratory organs like gills, book gills, book lungs or tracheal system are found in phylum
questions.solution: They have an organ-system level of organization. They are bilaterally symmetrical, triploblastic, segmented and coelomate animals. The body of arthropods is covered by a chitinous exoskeleton. The body consists of a head, thorax and abdomen. They have jointed appendages (arthros-joint, poda-appendages). Respiratory organs are gills, book gills, book lungs or tracheal system. The circulatory system is of open type. Sensory organs like antennae, eyes (compound and simple), statocysts or balancing organs are present. Excretion takes place through malpighian tubules.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Select the incorrect statement.
options: Digestive system is complete in Aschelminthes and Echinodermata but not in Platyhelminthes.
Segmentation is present in Annelida and Arthropoda but absent in Chordata.
Organ system level of organisation is found in Aschelminthes and Annelida but not in Ctenophora.

questions.solution:
Metameric segmentation is found in annelids, arthropods and chordates. In metameric segmentation, there is a linear repetition of body parts where each repeated unit is called somite (metamere).

In earthworms, the successive somites are essentially similar, but they are dissimilar in different body regions of a crayfish or insect. Metamerism is conspicuous both externally in annelids. It is mostly external in arthropods and internal in humans and in other chordates (vertebrate, body muscles, some blood vessels and nerves).

questions.solution:

Examples: Pleurobrachia and Ctenoplana.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:

(ii) Sponge cells are devoid of cellulose cell walls.
(iii) The life cycle of sponges includes swimming ciliated larval stages resembling those of other marine animals. Sponges are sessile and digestion is very simple without any apparent way of capturing food or eliminating wastes.

questions.solution: The diagram represents the class Cyclostomata. The body is elongated, eel-like with median fins and cartilaginous fin ray. The paired appendages are absent, tail is diphycercal. Skin is soft, smooth and containing unicellular mucous glands, but no scales are present. Notochord persists throughout life. Imperfect neural arches over notochord represent rudimentary vertebrae. questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is the correct combination of the class of vertebrates and properties exhibited by it?
options: Three chambered heart: Amphibia and Aves
questions.solution: Most of the members of class Chondrichthyes (cartilaginous fishes) are viviparous, while those belonging to class Osteichthyes (bony fishes) are oviparous. Amphibians cannot maintain a constant internal temperature (poikilothermic), while mammals can maintain a constant internal temperature (homeothermic). questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Schizocoelomates and enterocoelomates are
questions.solution:
The presence or absence of coelom is an important basis of classifications in animals. Coelom refers to a large fluid-filled space lying between two outer body wall and inner digestive tube.

Schizocoelom arises from a mesodermal split. This body cavity is formed from blocks of mesoderm around the gut that enlarge and hollow out. Example- animals belonging to the Phyla Annelida, Mollusca and Arthropoda. Enterocoelom arises from out pocketing of the embryonic gut (endoderm). This type of body cavity is formed by out pocketing of the primitive gut that breaks off and forms the coelom. Example- animals belonging to the Phyla Echinodermata and Chordata.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following statements is incorrect about metagenesis?
options: Alternation of asexual and sexual phases in the life cycle of Obelia is called metagenesis
Metagenesis is similar to alternation of generations as found in plants
Both the medusa and polyp are diploid
Medusa is the sexual phase and polyp is the asexual phase
questions.solution:
Metagenesis is the alternation of generations between sexual and asexual reproduction, but not similar to alternation of generations as found in plants. In plants, the alternation of generations occurs between a diploid sporophyte and a haploid gametophyte, and not between sexual and asexual reproduction.

Alternation of asexual and sexual phases in the life cycle of Obelia is called metagenesis. In Obelia, both the medusa(the motile stage) and polyp(the sessile stage) are diploid. Medusa is the sexual phase and polyp is the asexual phase.

The presence of the ventral nerve cord is characteristically seen in all invertebrates. The Annelida and Arthropoda are invertebrates and hence all three pose the ventral nerve cord with the anterior region connecting cerebral ganglia and the posterior region connecting to the last abdominal ganglion.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following statements is correct for the phylum whose organisms are characterized by the presence of a dorsal hollow nerve cord and paired pharyngeal gill slits?
options: In all protochordates, notochord extends from head to tail region and is persistent throughout the life.
The members of the class to which Myxine belongs show the presence of a sucking and circular mouth without jaws.
Members of the class Osteichthyes show the presence of an air bladder, a streamlined body and four gills covered by operculum.
The members of the class to which the frog belongs are cold blooded, show external fertilization and a three chambered heart i.e. one auricle and two ventricles.
questions.solution: The phylum whose organisms are characterized by the presence of a dorsal hollow nerve cord and paired pharyngeal gill slits is Phylum Chordata. It is divided into three sub-phyla i.e. Urochordata, Cephalochordata and Vertebrata. Urochordates and Cephalochordates are together referred to as protochordates. Urochordates show the presence of notochord only in the larval tail. Cephalochordates show the presence of notochord from head to tail and is persistent throughout life. Myxine belongs to the class Cyclostomata. Its members show the presence of sucking circular mouth without jaws. The body is devoid of scales and paired fins. Members of the class Osteichthyes show the presence of an air bladder, a streamlined body and four pairs of gills covered by operculum on each side. Frog belongs to the Class Amphibia. The members of this class are cold blooded, show external fertilization and have a three chambered heart i.e. two auricles and one ventricle.

questions.solution:
In this diagram I includes II which includes III which includes IV. Thus group IV should be a sub group of group III which should be a sub group of II which should be a sub group of I.

In option ii, Animals with radial symmetry are present in Phylum Cnidaria, Phylum Ctenophora and Phylum Echinodermata. Animals with calcareous ossicles are present in Phylum Echinodermata. Animals with rasping organs called radula are present in Mollusca which is not included in Echinodermata.

In option iv. Animals with notochord during embryonic stages are included in Phylum Chordata. Animals with well- defined jaws are present in Gnathostomata which is division under Phylum Chordata. Animals with 12 pairs of cranial nerves are amniotes includes in Class Reptilia, Aves and Mammalia included under division Gnathostomata. questions.q: Hydra possesses
questions.solution: Hydra can also reproduce sexually. Sexual reproduction is seasonal, the season depending on species, but generally summer or autumn. There is no free sexual medusoid stage and gonads develop on the column of the polyp. These gonads are not really true organs, but accumulations of gametes produced from interstitial cells that cause swellings in& the epidermis on the sides of the column. Usually, several testes develop on the anterior half of the column and usually one ovary on the posterior half of the column. A thinning of the epidermis occurs over the testis, developing into a& nipple-like papilla which eventually ruptures, shedding ripe sperm from the testes. The spermatozoa are flagellated and swim towards ripe ovaries. In a ripe ovary, the epidermis has ruptured to form a pore through which the sperm can& swim to reach the oocyte. The ovary begins as a group of cells, but the larger of these cells eventually engulfs the& others to form a single oocyte or egg cell.

Paired pharyngeal gill slits at least in embryonic stage
questions.solution: Ascidia is a urochordate with an open circulatory system and is a protochordate. Pristis is a cartilaginous sawfish and is jawed vertebrae bear fins. Hyla is a tree frog with a bony skeleton. Calotes is a garden lizard with bony skeleton all these animals bears the paired pharyngeal gill slits at least in the embryonic stage (chordates have the dorsal, hollow nerve cord).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following incorrect about Ichthyophis?
questions.solution: Ichthyophis is a limbless amphibian. It belongs to the Order Apoda. External fertilization, oviparous nature and absence of exoskeleton are its features.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Radula and water vascular system are found in organism A and organism B respectively. Identify A and B.
options: A - Tusk shell, B - Sea urchin
questions.solution:
Radula in Mollusca - It is a file like rasping organ in the mouth that helps in feeding.
Examples: Pila (Apple snail), Pinctada (Pearl oyster), Sepia& (Cuttlefish), Loligo (Squid), Octopus (Devilfish), Aplysia (Seahare), Dentalium (Tusk shell) and Chaetopleura (Chiton).

A most important feature of Echinodermates: Presence of water vascular system. It performs the function of locomotion, capture and transport of food.
Examples: Asterias (Star fish), Echinus (Sea urchin), Antedon& (Sea lily), Cucumaria (Sea cucumber) and Ophiura (Brittle star).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Four characters (a-d) are given below. Which two are CORRECT about phylum arthropoda?

(i) It is the largest phylum of animal kingdom.
(ii) One third of all named species on earth are arthropods.
(iii) They are bilaterally symmetrical, triploblastic and segmented animals.
(iv) The body is covered by calcareous exoskeleton.
questions.solution: Phylum Arthropoda is the largest phylum of animal kingdom. These include two third of all the animals on the earth. Majority of animals in this phylum are insects. 'Arthros' means joins and 'poda' means feet and hence these animals have jointed appendages. The body is divided into head, thorax and abdomen. These animals have proper organ systems, triploblastic body and are Eucoelomates. Their body is covered by exoskeleton made up of chitin.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is not a characteristic feature of nematodes?
questions.solution: Nematodes belong to Phylum Aschelminthes. The main distinguishing feature is that sexes are separate. These are known as roundworms as they show presence of body cavity. These show well presence of organ system and hence digestive system is also complete. These can be free living or parasitic in nature. The parasites can be in ectoparasites or endoparasites depending on whether they are on the host or inside the host.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements and select the true ($\left(T)\right)$~or false ($\left(F)\right)$ statement.

$A .$~The notochord is an ectodermal derived rod-like structure in chordates.

$B .$ Platyhelminthes are triploblastic and pseudocoelomate animals.

$C .$ The alternation of generation in Obelia is called Metastasis.

$D . In$ Ctenophora, only sexual mode of reproduction is observed.
options:
A B C D
F F T T

A B C D
T T F F

A B C D
F F F T

A B C D
T F F F
questions.solution:
Notochord is amesodermally derived rod like structure in chordates.

Platyhelminthes are triploblastic and acoelomate animals. Aschelminthes are triploblastic and pesudocoelomate animals. The alternation of generation in Obelia is called Metagenesis.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Match the name of the animal (column I), with one characteristic (column II), and the phylum/class (column III) to which it belongs.
options:
Column I Column II Column III
Limulus Body covered by chitinous exoskeleton Pisces

Column I Column II Column III
Adamsia Radially symmetrical Porifera

Column I Column II Column III
Ichthyophis Terrestrial Reptilia
questions.solution: Limulus belongs to phylum Arthropoda and its body is covered by a chitinous exoskeleton. Adamsia belongs to Phylum Coelenterata and is radially symmetrical. Petromyzon is an ectoparasite and belongs to class Cyclostomata. Icthyophis is a limbless amphibian.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following statements is incorrect about metagenesis?
options: Alternation of asexual and sexual phases in the life cycle of Obelia is called metagenesis
Metagenesis is similar to alternation of generations as found in plants
Both the medusa and polyp are diploid
Medusa is the sexual phase and polyp is the asexual phase
questions.solution:
Metagenesis is the alternation of generations between sexual and asexual reproduction, but not similar to alternation of generations as found in plants. In plants, the alternation of generations occurs between a diploid sporophyte and a haploid gametophyte, and not between sexual and asexual reproduction.

Alternation of asexual and sexual phases in the life cycle of Obelia is called metagenesis. In Obelia, both the medusa(the motile stage) and polyp(the sessile stage) are diploid. Medusa is the sexual phase and polyp is the asexual phase.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of these classes doesn't belong to the same superclass?
questions.solution: Chordates are further classified as protochordate and vertebrates. Protochordate includes urochordates and cephalochordates. Vertebrates are classified as superclass Pisces and superclass Tetrapods. Tetrapods are divided into classes Amphibians, Reptiles, Aves and Mammals. Pisces include Chondrichthyes and Osteichthyes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the sponge is given as a gift in Japan?
questions.solution: Euplectella belongs to phylum Porifera. These organisms show the presence of pores all over the body. The water canal system is the characteristic feature of these organisms. These show specialized cells known as chaonocytes i.e. collar cells. Example: Spongilla, Leucosolenia, Euplectella etc. Euplectella is known as Venus flower basket and is given as a gift in Japan during weddings.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Amphibians share with reptiles all of the following characters except
questions.solution: Amphibians and Reptiles show direct development. Both of them have a ventral heart. They both are cold blooded (poikiolothermic). They also have both male and female reproductive organs in separate individuals. They produce young ones by laying eggs which are hatched after they have been laid by the parent.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Triploblastic, unsegmented, acoelomate exhibit bilateral symmetry reproducing both asexually and sexually, with some parasitic forms. This description is characteristic of the phylum
questions.solution: Triploblastic means having three germ layers: ectoderm, mesoderm, and endoderm. This is seen for the first time in the phylum Platyhelminthes. These are flatworms that exhibit bilateral symmetry. These do not show any body cavity hence are acoelomates. Example: Tapeworms, liver flukes etc. These reproduce by asexual and sexual manner. Thus only this phylum is triploblastic but are acoelomates.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the features given below and select the option for animals which correctly describes the features mentioned:

I. All are exclusively marine, triploblastic, coelomate organism with a water vascular system.

II.A small group of worm-like marine animals with the organ system levels of the organization.

III. The body is covered by a calcareous shell and is unsegmented with a distinct head, muscular foot, and visceral hump.

IV. Triploblastic, pesudocoelomate animals in which alimentary canal is complete with a well developed muscular pharynx.
questions.solution: Echinodermata are the exclusively marine, triploblastic, coelomate organisms with a water vascular system (Asterius, ophiura). In Mollusca body is covered by calcareous shell and is unsegmented with a distinct head, muscular foot, and visceral hump (Pila, Sepia). Hemichordates are a small group of worm-like marine animals with organ system level of organization (Balanoglossus, Saccoglossus).& Triploblastic, pesudocoelomate animals in which alimentary canal is complete with a well developed muscular pharynx is seen in Aschelmenthis with Ascaris as example.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The "nervous system" of Hydra consists of
questions.solution: Hydra belonging to the phylum Cnidaria is a genus of fresh-water organisms. They are generally found in the tropical and temperate regions. A nerve net found in Hydra serves as a simple nervous system that connects photoreceptors and touch sensitive nerve cells. These cells are found in the body wall and tentacles. Brain and muscles are absent in Hydra. Also, the nervous system is not as complex found in higher animal nervous systems. The nerve cells of hydra are nonpolarized and signal can move in any direction.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following statements about all the four of Spongilla, Leech, Dolphin and Penguin is CORRECT?
options: Penguin is homoeothermic while the remaining three are poikilothermic.
Leech is a freshwater form while all others are marine.
Spongilla has special collared cells called choanocytes, not found in the remaining three.
All of them shows bilateral symmetry.
questions.solution:
Penguin is a flightless bird belonging to the group of Aves and is a homeotherm. Dolphin is an aquatic mammal that gives birth to live young ones and found in both freshwater and marine water. It is also homeotherm.

Leech is a segmented parasite under the phylum Annelida majorly found in the freshwater habitat. They are hermaphrodites and poikilothermic.

Spongilla is a freshwater sponge found in lakes in slow streams. They remain attached to the rock and logs surface and filter water using their special cells called choanocytes. It obtains it nutrient through this process.

The symmetry of leech, penguin and dolphin is bilateral and that is Spongilla is asymmetrical.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Find the odd one.
questions.solution: Sea fan is Gorgonia. It belongs to Phylum Colenterata. These have tissue level of organization and are diploblastic organisms. These also show presence of Cnidoblasts which are stinging cells and thus are cnidoblasts. Sea lily is Antedon, Sea cucumber is Cucumaria and Sea urchin is Echinus. These three belong to Phylum Echinodermata. These animals have spiny body (Echino means spines and derma is skin). These also show presence of water vascular system.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following is matching set of phylum and its three examples?
questions.solution: Spongilla and euplectella belongs to the phylum Porifera and pennatula belongs to the class Anthozoa, phylum Coelenterata. Physalia and aurelia belongs to class Hydrozoa and Schopozoa, phylum Coelenterata and limulus belong to the phylum Arthropoda. Planaria and schistosoma belongs to phylum Platyhelmenthis and enterobius is a round worm belonging to phylum Aschelmenthis. Loligo, teredo and octopus belongs to the phylum Mollusca. These are known as Mollusc because of shell like covering present. These are bilaterally symmetrical, have three germ layers band have a body cavity too. The body is not segmented but shows presence of distinct head, muscular foot and visceral hump. A soft mantle is seen over the visceral hump which plays a role in respiration and excretion.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The spongocoel of Leucosolenia is lined with
questions.solution: Leucosolenia belong to Phylum Porifera. These are simplest animals as they show cellular organization. These are asymmetrical with no body cavity and are diploblastic. These show presence of pores all over the body. The two layers present are outer pinacoderm and inner choanoderm which encloses the spongocoel. These show presence of various cells for different functions. Choanocytes are seen on the choanoderm lining the spongocoeal. These are collar cells and are responsible for water transport through water canal system. The body also shows presence of spicules. Amoebocytes are totipotent cells in porifera.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following represents the correct combination without any exception?
options:
Characteristics Class
Mouth ventral; 5 -7 pairs of gills; skin with placoid scales; persistent notochord Chondrichthyes

Characteristics Class
Sucking and circular mouth; jaws present, integument without scales; paired appendages Cyclostomata

Characteristics Class
Body covered with feathers; skin moist and glandular; hindlimbs form wings; lungs with air sacs Aves

Characteristics Class
Mammary gland; hair on body; pinnae; two pairs of limbs Mammalia
questions.solution: Class Pisces is divided into two groups: Chondrichthyes and Osteichthyes. Chondrichthyes are cartilaginous fishes. These have a ventral mouth, placoid scales while air bladder and operculum are absent. Thus they differ from Osteichthyes. These do not show 5-7 pairs of gill slits. Cyclostomatas are chordates with circular mouth but jaws are absent and hence are known as Agnathas. Class Aves belongs to tetrapods in which fore limbs are modified into wings. All mammals have mammary glands, hair on body and two pairs of limbs. All mammals have pinnae except aquatic mammals.&

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Select the option with a correct representation of an animal to the below-mentioned class of vertebrates:

I. The jawless animal in which the body is devoid of scales and paired fins.

II. They have four pairs of gills that are covered by an operculum.

III. The body is covered by dry and cornified skin, epidermal scales or scutes.

IV. Skin is dry without glands and long bones are hollow with air cavities.
questions.solution: Cyclostomata such as lamprey is jawless and the body is devoid of scales and paired fins. Osteichthyes such as clarius, have four pairs of gills which are covered by an operculum. In calotes, the Reptiles, the body is covered by dry and cornified skin, epidermal scales or scutes.& Neophron, an Egyptian vulture& the skin is dry without glands and long bones are hollow with air cavities.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which is not correctly matched?
questions.solution: Annelida possess true coelom. Their coelom is schizocoelic in origin (i.e., it is formed by the splitting of embryonic mesoderm), thus they can also be called schizocoelomata.& Phylum Echinodermata and Chordata have enterocoelom, where the& coelom is formed by the splitting of endoderm.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In the diploblastic animals:
options: Mesoderm and mesoglea both are absent
Mesoderm is present but mesoglea is absent
Mesoderm is absent but mesoglea is present
Mesoderm and mesoglea both are present.
questions.solution: Animals in which the cells are arranged in two embryonic layers, external ectoderm and an internal endoderm, are called diploblastic animals, e.g., coelenterates. An undifferentiated layer, mesoglea, is present in between the ectoderm and the endoderm.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following organ never helps in oxygenation of blood in any vertebrate, at any stage of their life?
questions.solution:
Vertebrates such as amphibians have 3-chambered heart, muscular, myogenic heart with two atria and single ventricle. In amphibians, the left atrium receives oxygenated blood from the gills/lungs/skin and the right atrium gets the deoxygenated blood from other body parts.
In amniota group, i.e. reptiles, birds and mammals, respiration is mainly pulmonary, in fishes it is through gills.

In vertebrates, the kidney is mainly involved in osmoregulation and excretion.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In Platyhelminthes, the digestive system is incomplete because
options: it absorbs food from general body surface
it has suckers and hooks in parasitic form
it has only one opening that serves as mouth and anus
questions.solution: Animal kingdom consists of two phylas. Phylum non chordates and chordates. Non chordates consist of Porifera, Colenterates, Ctenophora, Platyhelminthes, Aschelminthes, Annelids, Arthropods, Molluscs, Echinodematas. Hemichordata etc. Platyhelminthes involves flatworms as they do not have body cavity. The body consists of organs but no organ systems. Thus digestive system is also incomplete. It means the system consists of only one opening that serves as both mouth and anus. This is seen in animals like hydra etc.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following is a matching pair of a body feature and the animal possessing it?
options: Pharyngeal gill slits absent during embryonic development - Chameleon
questions.solution: The ventral nerve cord is found in insects and is functionally equivalent to the vertebrate spinal cord. This kind of nervous system is found in leeches and some of the annelids and arthropods. The scorpion possesses a dorsal heart, Post anal tail is usually seen in cobras belonging to the phylum Chordata. Pharyngeal gill slits are found in the embryos of all vertebrates due to their common ancestors, the fish, who were the first one to have these structures.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Metagenesis is seen in:
questions.solution: Cnidarians exhibit two basic body forms called polyp and medusa. The former is a sessile and cylindrical form like Hydra, Adamsia, etc. whereas, the latter is umbrella-shaped and free-swimming like Aurelia or jelly fish. Those cnidarians which exist in both forms exhibit alternation of generation (metagenesis), i.e., polyps produce medusae asexually and medusae form the polyps sexually (e.g., Obelia).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the characteristics given below of a chordate:

a) two-chambered heart
b) poikilotherms
c) exclusively marine
d) oviparous with direct development
e) separate sexes

Which of the following possess all of the above features?
questions.solution:
Class Osteichthyes:

It includes both marine and fresh water fishes with bony endoskeleton. Their body is streamlined. Mouth is mostly terminal.. They have four pairs of gills which are covered by an operculum on each side. Skin is covered with cycloid/ctenoid scales. Air bladder is present which regulates buoyancy. Heart is twochambered (one auricle and one ventricle). They are cold-blooded animals. Sexes are separate. Fertilisation is usually external. They are mostly oviparous and development is direct. Examples: Marine – Exocoetus (Flying fish), Hippocampus (Sea horse); Freshwater – Labeo (Rohu), Catla (Katla), Clarias (Magur); Aquarium – Betta (Fighting fish), Pterophyllum (Angel fish).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In which of the following organisms, self-fertilization is seen?
questions.solution: Fishes are chordates and roundworms belong to the phylum Aschelminthes. In these two organisms, the sexes are separate hence self-fertilization is not possible. Earthworms are hermaphrodite as both the sexes are present in the same body. Earthworms still do not show self-fertilization as the maturing times of both the sex organs are different. In earthworms, the male gonads mature earlier than female gonads. This is known as a protandry condition. Thus it shows cross-fertilization. In liver fluke both cross and self-fertilization is seen as they are hermaphrodites. It shows both the sex organs and thus self-fertilization is commonly seen.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A completely four-chambered heart is present in
options: all reptiles, all birds and all mammals
some reptiles, all birds and all mammals
no reptiles, all birds and all mammals
some reptiles, some birds and all mammals
questions.solution: Chordates show a closed circulatory system i.e. proper system of heart and blood vessels. The heart has evolved from two chambers to four chambers. Pisces shows the presence of two chambers: one ventricle and one auricle. Amphibians show three chambers: two auricles and one ventricle due to which mixed blood flows in the heart. Reptiles like crocodiles, birds and mammals show four chambers (two auricles and two ventricles) and thus proper closed circulation is seen.& Except for crocodilians, which have a four-chambered heart, all reptiles have a three-chambered heart consisting of two atria and one ventricle.&

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Absence of circulatory system in Hydra is compensated by
questions.solution: Hydra is relatives of corals and jellyfish. All these species are members of the phylum Cnidaria characterized by symmetrical bodies crowned by 10-12 tentacles and an opening called a gastrovascular cavity. This class of organisms don't have a specialized circulatory system. They have a thin layer of cells which when coming in contact with water absorb the nutrients and oxygen required by the body.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following character is unique to Mollusca?
questions.solution: Molluscs are terrestrial or aquatic (marine or fresh water) having an organ-system level of organisation. They are bilaterally symmetrical, triploblastic and coelomate animals. Body is covered by a calcareous shell and is unsegmented with a distinct head, muscular foot and visceral hump. A soft and spongy layer of skin forms a mantle over the visceral hump. The space between the hump and the mantle is called the mantle cavity in which feather like gills are present. They have respiratory and excretory functions. The anterior head region has sensory tentacles. The mouth contains a file-like rasping organ for feeding, called radula.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The organism where the adult shows pentaradial symmetry, while the larval forms shows biradial symmetry is
questions.solution: Phylum Echinodermata: These animals have an endoskeleton of calcareous ossicles and, hence, the name Echinodermata (Spiny bodied). All are marine with organ-system level of organisation. The adult echinoderms are radially symmetrical but larvae are bilaterally symmetrical.& Examples: Asterias (Star fish), Echinus (Sea urchin), Antedon (Sea lily), Cucumaria (Sea cucumber) and Ophiura (Brittle star).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The members of which of the following phyla are exclusively marine?
questions.solution: Echinoderms are invertebrates with spiny skin, water vascular system and a simple nervous system. This phylum is majorly a marine group and found in all oceans. They are not found in freshwater or terrestrial surfaces. There are around 7000 species of this group which found exclusively in marine environments. The other three phyla habitat various ecologies such as freshwater, terrestrial environments and marine waters.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
How many statements are correct regarding the organisms shown in following figure?



a) It belongs to the class Cyclostomata.
b) It has 6 to 15 pairs of gill slits.
c) Their body is devoid of scales.
d) In males, pelvic fins bear claspers.
questions.solution:
The given picture is of a jawless vertebrate called Petromyzon.
It belongs to the class Cyclostomata and they have an elongated body bearing 6-15 pairs of gill slits for respiration.& Their body is devoid of scales and paired fins.
Male cartilaginous fish have claspers formed from the posterior portion of their pelvic fin which serve as is used to channel semen into the female's cloaca. Such fish belong to the class Chondrichthyes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following characters stands true for Antedon?
options: Spiny-bodied and organ level of organisation
Mouth on the dorsal side and anus on the ventral side
questions.solution: Antedon or sea lily belongs to the phylum Echinodermata.& All are marine with an organ-system level of organisation. The adult echinoderms are radially symmetrical but larvae are bilaterally symmetrical. They are triploblastic and coelomate animals. The digestive system is complete with the mouth on the lower (ventral) side and anus on the upper (dorsal) side.&

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following animals is not a pair of poikilotherms?
questions.solution: Fishes (like Labeo, Torpedo, Pristis, Carcharodon, Scoliodon, Trygon), Amphibians (Rana) and Reptiles (Naja) are poikilotherms but& Pteropus (mammal) is a homeotherm.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following set of animals have homeothermic, monocondylic skull, twelve pairs of cranial nerves, pneumatic bones, and four-chambered heart condition?
questions.solution: Aves are warm-blooded or homeothermic animals. They have single occipital condyle bone in the skull, called monocondylic. They possess twelve pairs of cranial nerves and a four-chambered heart. example:& Psittacula (Parrot), Neophron (Vulture), Columba (Pigeon).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following groups of three animals each are correctly matched with their characteristic morphological feature?
options:
Animals Morphological feature
Centipede, Prawn, Sea urchin Joined appendages

Animals Morphological feature
Scorpion, Spider, Cockroach Ventral solid central nervous system

Animals Morphological feature
Cockroach, Locust , Taenia Metameric segmentation

Animals Morphological feature
Liver fluke, Sea anemone,Sea cucumber Bilateral symmetry
questions.solution: Scorpion, Spider and Cockroaches are Arthropods and thus are Non-chordates. All non-chordates show presence of ventral nerve cord. In option (B), Centipede and prawn show jointed appendages as these are Arthropods but Sea urchin is an Echinoderm. In option (C), Cockroaches and Locust are Arthropods and hence body is divisible into head, thorax and abdomen while Taenia are flat worms and belong to Phylum Platyhelminthes and thus segmentation is absent. In option (D), Liver fluke shows bilateral symmetry. Sea anemone is Coelenterate and thus shows radial symmetry while sea cucumber belongs to Echinodermata which shows bilateral symmetry in larval stage and radial symmetry in adult stage.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
How many animals from the following are warm-blooded with 4-chambered heart and oviparous condition?

[Corvus, Struthio, Macropus, Ornithorhynchus, Balaenoptera, Pteropus, Delphinus, Psittacula, Chelone, Calotes, Crocodilus]
questions.solution: Aves or birds are warm-blooded animals with 4-chambered heart and oviparous conditions. These include Corvus (Crow), Struthio (Ostrich), Psittacula (Parrot). Crocodile is a reptile with a four-chambered heart.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following animals belongs to phylum Coelenterata?
questions.solution:
A sea pen is Gorgonia. it belongs to Phylum Coelenterata. This is also known as Phylum Cnidaria due to the presence of Cnidoblast cells. These are stinging cells present on the tentacles. This phylum includes tissue level organisation and are acoelomates. Metagenesis is the characteristic feature seen in many Coelenterates.

Sea horse is a chordate (Osteichthyes). Sea hare and sea cucumber belong to Phylum Mollusca.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: An acoelomate animal with bilateral symmetry is:
questions.solution:
Animals possessing coelom are called coelomates, e.g., annelids, molluscs, arthropods, echinoderms, hemichordates and chordates. In some animals, the body cavity is not lined by mesoderm, instead, the mesoderm is present as scattered pouches in between the ectoderm and endoderm. Such a body cavity is called pseudocoelom and the animals possessing them are called pseudocoelomates, e.g.,
aschelminthes. The animals in which the body cavity is absent are called acoelomates, e.g., Platyhelminthes.

They have dorso-ventrally flattened body, hence are called flatworms. Flatworms are bilaterally symmetrical, triploblastic and acoelomate animals with organ level of organisation.
Examples: Taenia (Tapeworm), Fasciola (Liver fluke).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following feature is common among Nereis, Pheretima and Hirudinaria?
options: Well developed clitellum for cocoon formation
Chitinous setae and parapodia for locomotion
questions.solution:
Nereis-Clitellum absent, setae and parapodia present and closed circulatory system.

Pheretima-Clitellum well developed, only chitinous setae and closed circulatory system

Hirudinaria-Temporary clitellum, setae and parapodia absent and open circulatory system.

All the three are coelomates and are metamerically segmented animals.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following organisms is radially symmetrical?
questions.solution: Radial Symmetry: A radial animal has a top and a bottom (or an oral and aboral side), but has no head end or rear end and no left or right.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A file-like rasping organ for feeding is observed in:
questions.solution: Molluscs are terrestrial or aquatic (marine or fresh water) having an organ-system level of organisation. They are bilaterally symmetrical, triploblastic and coelomate animals. The mouth contains a file-like rasping organ for feeding, called radula.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Select the correct match about vertebrates with their features:
options: Electric organ of Torpedo → modified muscles on dorsal side
Sting of Trygon → modified pelvic fin
questions.solution: In Scoliodon → Dog fish, the teeth are modified placoid scales which are backwardly directed. In Trygon → Sting ray, the dorsal fin is modified into the sting.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Select the correct set of animals of class Mammalia.
questions.solution: Class mammals belong to Superclass Tetrapods of Vertebrates. These animals are so called due to mammary glands. These animals are seen in all habitats. Example: whale is seen in water, Bat has aerial habitat while kangaroo and hippopotamus are land mammals.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
How many from the following phylum has external fertilisation with indirect development?

{Porifera, Ctenophora, Echinodermata, Hemichordata}
questions.solution:
External fertilisation with indirect development is present in aquatic animals which belongs to phylum → Ctenophora with cydipidd larva, Echinodermata with the different larva and Hemichordata with tornaria larva.

In Porifera, fertilisation is internal and development is indirect having a larval stage which is morphologically distinct from the adult.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Ascaris is characterized by the
options: presence of neither true coelom nor metamerism.
presence of true coelom but absence of metamerism.
presence of both true coelom and metamerism.
absence of true coelom but presence of metamerism.
questions.solution: Ascaris belong to Phylum Aschelminthes. The main distinguishing feature is that sexes are separate. These are known as roundworms as they show presence of body cavity. These show well presence of organ system and hence digestive system is also complete. These can be free living or parasitic in nature. A B C D

(b) Endoderm Mesoderm Mesoglea Ectoderm
(c) Mesoderm Mesoglea Ectoderm Endoderm

questions.solution:
Animals in which the cells are arranged in two embryonic layers, an external ectoderm and an internal endoderm, are called diploblastic. An undifferentiated layer, mesoglea, is present in between the ectoderm and the endoderm.

Those animals in which the developing embryo has a third germinal layer, mesoderm, in between the ectoderm and endoderm, are called triploblastic animals (platyhelminthes to chordates).
